projects.title: The Henderson Home
projects.cardSummary: A Stiebel Eltron air-to-water heat pump running underfloor heating, active ceiling panels, cooling and hot water, with heat recovery ventilation and fire sprinklers throughout. Twelve months in, it has far exceeded expectations for health and comfort.
projects.heroSummary: A home where heating, cooling, hot water and fresh air work as one quiet, efficient system.

heroImage.alt: Exterior courtyard of The Henderson Home in Wānaka

storyParagraphs: After years of cold, draughty homes and rising power bills, the owners wanted a home that felt consistently healthy and comfortable without demanding excessive energy.

The answer began with the building itself: high insulation levels, an airtight wrap and triple glazing reduce the load before any heating is switched on. Optum then sized one integrated system around the way the home would actually perform.
projects.featuresSummary: Every component was selected to do its job quietly while supporting the performance of the whole home.

features.title: Heating & hot water
features.description: A 7kW Stiebel Eltron air-to-water heat pump supplies low-temperature space heating and a 400L hot-water cylinder.

features.title: Underfloor & active ceilings
features.description: Underfloor loops warm the concrete and tiled zones, while active ceiling panels give bedrooms a faster response.

features.title: Cooling & fresh air
features.description: The heat pump reverses for summer cooling, supported by balanced heat-recovery ventilation delivering filtered, dry air.

features.title: Protection & water quality
features.description: Concealed residential fire sprinklers and whole-home UV filtration add protection without compromising the architecture.

projects.title: Camp Glenorchy
projects.cardSummary: Solar thermal collectors, ground source heating, underfloor and full plumbing and drainage for New Zealand's most sustainable visitor accommodation. Named Project of the Year at the 2018 Master Plumbers Awards.
projects.award: Project of the Year · Master Plumbers 2018
projects.heroSummary: Integrated renewable heating, water and drainage services for a visitor retreat built to demonstrate better environmental performance.

heroImage.alt: Camp Glenorchy eco retreat beneath the surrounding mountains

storyParagraphs: Camp Glenorchy was conceived as a practical demonstration of resource-efficient accommodation—comfortable for guests while reducing demand on energy and water.

Optum's work brought heating, solar collection, plumbing and drainage into one coordinated services package. The system needed to perform in an alpine climate while staying true to the project's environmental intent.
projects.featuresSummary: A coordinated approach made the renewable systems part of the building rather than an addition to it.

features.title: Solar thermal
features.description: Roof-mounted collectors harvest solar energy to reduce the demand associated with water heating.

features.title: Ground-source heating
features.description: Ground-source technology provides an efficient foundation for space heating in Glenorchy's demanding climate.

features.title: Underfloor comfort
features.description: Low-temperature underfloor heating delivers even warmth without interrupting the architecture or guest experience.

features.title: Plumbing & drainage
features.description: Complete plumbing and drainage services were coordinated across the retreat as part of the wider sustainability strategy.

projects.title: Hidden Island
projects.cardSummary: A 500m²-plus home run by a 30kW ground source heat pump with zoned underfloor heating, thermal storage, 5kW solar PV and wastewater treatment, designed for efficiency at scale.
projects.heroSummary: A large alpine home whose heating, energy and wastewater systems were designed for efficiency at scale.

heroImage.alt: Hidden Island architectural home beneath the Remarkables at Jacks Point

projects.storyHeadingBefore: High comfort, without energy use growing with the
storyParagraphs: A home of more than 500m² creates a substantial heating and energy challenge, particularly at the foot of the Remarkables.

Working with the homeowner and project managers from consultation through completion, Optum designed the services as one coordinated system: ground-source heating, zoned distribution, thermal storage, on-site generation and wastewater treatment.
projects.featuresSummary: The system balances generous comfort with deliberate control over when and where energy is used.

features.title: 30kW ground source
features.description: A Kensa ground-source heat pump draws stable low-grade energy from the ground to serve the home's heating demand.

features.title: Zoned underfloor heating
features.description: Separate underfloor zones with Heatmiser controls allow different parts of the home to be managed independently.

features.title: Thermal storage & solar PV
features.description: A Rotex thermal store works alongside a 5kW solar array and Power Genius distribution to make better use of generated energy.

features.title: Wastewater treatment
features.description: Two Biolytix treatment systems complete the integrated response to the site's servicing requirements.
